text: PART 1 Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai (MCGM / BMC) The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), officially known as MCGM, is the civic body responsible for the infrastructure and civic administration of Mumbai. It is one of the richest municipal corporations in India. Official Website: mcgm.gov.in Helpline: 1916 (BMC 24x7 Helpline) Jurisdiction: City of Mumbai (Island City + Suburbs + Extended Suburbs) Ward Offices: 24 administrative wards 1.1 Citizen Charter The BMC Citizen Charter defines the rights of citizens and the service standards the corporation commits to deliver. It covers response times, escalation paths, and redressal mechanisms. Core Citizen Rights • Right to receive civic services within defined time limits • Right to information about service status • Right to register grievances and receive acknowledgement • Right to appeal if services are denied • Right to clean public spaces, pothole-free roads, and functioning streetlights Key Services & Committed Timelines Service Committed

text: PART 2 Urban Governance & Government Schemes The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) administers several flagship schemes for urban development in India. Mumbai benefits from multiple central and state schemes. 2.1 Swachh Bharat Mission - Urban (SBM-U 2.0) SBM-U 2.0 (2021-2026) focuses on making cities 'Garbage Free' by targeting solid waste management, wastewater management, and plastic elimination. Key Objectives • Complete elimination of open defecation (ODF++) • 100% source segregation of waste (Wet, Dry, Hazardous) • Scientific processing of all solid waste generated • Remediation of all legacy dumpsites • Reduction of single-use plastics Mumbai Specific Implementation • Mumbai generates approximately 7,000-7,500 metric tonnes of waste daily • BMC manages waste through 3 processing sites: Deonar, Mulund, and Kanjurmarg • Wet waste: Goes to composting/biogas plants • Dry waste: Channeled to Material Recovery Facilities (MRF) • Hazardous: Sent to licensed facilities (Taloja) Citizen Responsibilities Under SBM • Segregate

text: 4.3 Heatwave Advisory Mumbai's coastal location moderates temperatures but heatwaves are increasing. NDMA defines heatwave as temperature 4.5 degrees Celsius above normal OR above 40 degrees Celsius in plains. Heatwave Dos and Don'ts • DO: Drink water every 30 minutes even without thirst; wear light-coloured loose cotton clothing; stay indoors 12pm-4pm • DO: Use ORS (Oral Rehydration Solution) if sweating heavily; cover head outdoors • DO NOT: Step out barefoot on hot ground; drink alcohol/tea/coffee in excess during heatwave (dehydrating) • DO NOT: Leave children or elderly or pets in parked vehicles Heat Stroke - Emergency Recognition • Signs: Body temp above 40C, no sweating despite heat, confusion, rapid pulse, red hot dry skin • Action: Call 108 immediately; move person to shade; apply ice/cold water to neck, armpits, groin • Do NOT give water to unconscious person Vulnerable Groups - Extra Care Needed • Elderly above 65 years •
